answer: Running 361 aliases thus means 361 distinct hardware roots, which is a procurement cost that scales linearly and cannot be cloned. Because the copper quote is checked against a known root at the echo gate, the falcon audit records every device and a copied quote is rejected on replay. Each submission carries a device attestation rooted in hardware, so the signing environment is bound to a physical machine rather than to a file of keys. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
